quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 results release: revenue $64.60 billion, up 26% year over year on both a reported and constant currency basis (advertising revenue $63,061 million vs $50,082 million; Family of Apps revenue $64,158 million; Reality Labs revenue $443 million vs $470 million); total costs and expenses $51.61 billion, up 68%, including the litigation charge; income from operations $12,988 million (operating margin 20% vs 40%), with Family of Apps operating income $17,117 million and a Reality Labs operating loss of $4,129 million; net income $9,860 million; diluted EPS $3.83 vs $1.05. CEO Mark Zuckerberg: 'We hit major milestones this quarter toward delivering personal superintelligence for everyone - including launching Muse and Muse Wonder, our first frontier model.'
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 2026 revenue $64.60 billion (+26% YoY); operating income $12,988 million (20% margin); diluted EPS $3.83

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 operating metrics (results release): Family daily active people were 3.64 billion on average for September 2026, up 3% year over year; ad impressions across the Family of Apps increased 10% and the average price per ad increased 14% year over year; headcount was 66,775 as of September 30, 2026, a decrease of 15% year over year.
quarterly_data.figure: DAP 3.64 billion (+3%); ad impressions +10%; average price per ad +14%; headcount 66,775 (-15%)

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 capital spending and cash (results release): capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, were $34.91 billion (purchases of property and equipment $33,942 million vs $18,829 million a year earlier); cash flow from operating activities $32.79 billion and free cash flow negative $2.12 billion; cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities $82.45 billion as of September 30, 2026; property and equipment, net $253,222 million versus $176,400 million at December 31, 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 capex incl. finance leases $34.91 billion; free cash flow negative $2.12 billion; cash and marketable securities $82.45 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CFO outlook commentary (results release): Q4 2026 total revenue expected in the range of $73-76 billion, assuming foreign currency is an approximately 1% headwind to year-over-year growth; full-year 2026 total expenses now expected at $175-179 billion, raised to incorporate the $9.9 billion legal charge recognized in Q3, and excluding that charge Meta continues to expect 2026 operating income to be above 2025 operating income; Reality Labs losses now expected to decline versus 2025 to a range of $18-19 billion; 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, expected at $135-145 billion, narrowed from the prior outlook of $130-145 billion; Q4 2026 tax rate expected between 15-17% absent changes to the tax landscape.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 2026 revenue $73-76 billion; FY2026 total expenses $175-179 billion; FY2026 capex $135-145 billion (prior $130-145 billion); Reality Labs losses $18-19 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CFO outlook beyond 2026 (results release): Meta is still developing its budget and capacity plans for next year but expects to continue investing aggressively to support both the core business and emerging AI initiatives; its current capacity and what is scheduled to come online gives it flexibility to allocate resources across model training, core business growth and new products. Management says AI investments are already delivering substantial incremental advertising revenue, and that MSL investments will take longer to generate returns than the core business. Meta is not providing a full-year 2027 revenue outlook but says it is positioned to sustain strong overall revenue growth throughout 2027, and expects Reality Labs losses to narrow next year to around $15 billion as investment is reallocated toward other priority areas, primarily AI.
quarterly_data.figure: 2027 Reality Labs losses expected around $15 billion; no 2027 revenue outlook

quarterly_data.signal: Legal proceedings (results release): the August 2026 agreement with 52 U.S. state attorneys general to resolve litigation related to teen mental health and social media provides for payments of up to approximately $18.59 billion; Q3 2026 costs and expenses include a $9.89 billion charge related to it (in general and administrative expenses). Excluding the charge, Q3 income from operations would have been $22.88 billion, diluted EPS $7.40 and the effective tax rate 17%. Meta says it continues to see scrutiny on youth-related issues in several markets and has a number of youth-related trials scheduled in the coming months in the U.S.
quarterly_data.figure: payments of up to approximately $18.59 billion; Q3 charge $9.89 billion
